reasoning_summary: 0001 OK: invokes the cited result [[Properties of Ordered Ring]] (5); legitimate appeal to an external lemma about ordered rings. 0002 OK: the content of that lemma, that every strictly positive integer multiple of a strictly positive element (here 1_D > 0_D, standard in an ordered integral domain) is strictly positive, so n.1_D > 0_D for all n in Z_{>0}. 0003 blank. 0004 OK: connective only. 0005 OK: Char D = p (p > 0) would require p.1_D = 0_D, contradicting 0002; hence no positive p can be the characteristic. 0006 blank. 0007 OK: connective only. 0008 OK: by the definition of characteristic (least positive p with p.1_D = 0_D, else 0), ruling out every positive p in 0005 forces Char D = 0. This discharges the first assertion of the theorem. 0009 blank. 0010 OK (standard, mildly compressed): g(n) = n.1_D is a ring homomorphism by the power/index laws, and its kernel is {n : n.1_D = 0_D} = {0} exactly because Char D = 0, so g is a monomorphism from Z into D. 0011 blank. 0012 OK: for integers m < p, p - m is a strictly positive integer, so p - m lies in Z_+. 0013 OK: (p - m).1_D = p.1_D - m.1_D by the index laws, and 0002 applied to the positive integer p - m gives p.1_D - m.1_D > 0_D. 0014 blank. 0015 OK: connective only. 0016 OK: 0013 rearranged in the compatible-ordering sense gives m.1_D < p.1_D, i.e. g(m) < g(p), so g is strictly order-preserving. 0017 blank. 0018 FAILS: this is where the argument does not deliver the stated theorem. Its stated conclusion ('g is a monomorphism from Z into D') is verbatim what 0010 already established, so the order work of 0012-0016 is never converted into a stated conclusion, and, decisively, neither this step nor any preceding step contains any argument for the two remaining parts of the claim: that g is ONTO D, and that g is the ONLY such monomorphism. Uniqueness would require the standard argument that any ring monomorphism h: Z -> D must send 1 to 1_D and hence n to n.1_D = g(n); nothing of the sort appears anywhere in the proof, and the cited [[Monomorphism from Total Ordering]] concerns order-preservation of a monomorphism, not uniqueness or surjectivity. 0019 FAILS (consequent): {{qed}} asserts the whole statement is proved, but only 'Char D = 0' and 'g is an order-preserving monomorphism into D' have been shown; the 'only ... onto' assertion of the problem statement is left entirely unaddressed. Overall: every individual inference 0001-0016 is sound and the characteristic-zero claim is correctly proved, but the proof is incomplete with respect to the theorem as stated, first failing at 0018.
